name: LenderLink
reason: Founder friction — offering May dates for meetings, making engagement unnecessarily difficult. Life is too short for reluctant founders. Company and thesis remain sound but the relationship dynamic is the earliest signal of how they'll run the company.

profile.whatTheyDo: Credit data exchange platform sitting between lenders, credit bureaus, and collection agencies in the Philippines. A single API accessing 36M+ verified credit records with a pay-per-hit model and revenue share back to contributors. 60% higher hit rate than incumbent bureaus at half the cost.
profile.whyFlagged: Textbook flow play. Credit data flows through LenderLink every time a lender queries a borrower. They're not the lender or bureau — they're the pipe. Switching means rebuilding integrations with 36M records. Philippines has 100M+ people, near-zero formal credit penetration, $14B consumer lending market growing 4x in a decade.
profile.founderProfile: All four founders were executives at Finscore, a telco-data credit risk company for the Philippines. Built it, scaled it, exited. Gold standard: serial winners with prior exit in the exact same domain, returning to the same market with a sharper thesis.
profile.revenueModel: Pay-per-hit (lenders only pay on a successful match) + revenue share to contributing lenders. Two-sided marketplace with structural switching costs on both sides.
profile.risks: Regulatory risk — credit data is sensitive. Each new market needs local contributors recruited from scratch. Incumbent credit bureaus could build competing APIs.
profile.macroTailwind: SEA digital lending growing fast — Philippines central bank actively pushing financial inclusion. Regional BNPL and neobank growth creating demand for credit data infrastructure.

name: Nexacore
reason: Wrong model for the lens. Melanie Hawgood (CEO) is impressive and the domain expertise is genuine (husband worked in insurance last-mile for years). AU contract via The Good Guys and Appliances Online is real traction. But the product is physical operations — drivers, device collection, repair, returns. That's a logistics business, not a pipe. Not raising capital currently. Passed April 2026.

profile.whatTheyDo: Insurtech Third Party Administrator (TPA) for device protection and extended warranty claims in Southeast Asia. Sits between insurers, telcos, and retailers on one side and device repair/replacement networks on the other. Every claim flows through the platform. Nexacore digitises and automates what is still largely a paper-based, manual claims process.
profile.whyFlagged: Classic TPA model — doesn't take insurance risk, just processes the flow. Every approved claim is a payment moving through Nexacore. Insurers integrate once; replacing them means rebuilding the entire claims workflow. Partnership with InsureMO (Nov 2025) unlocks rollout across UAE, India, AU, NZ, SG, MY simultaneously.
profile.founderProfile: Melanie Hawgood (CEO & Co-Founder) — insurance industry background, domain expert in device protection and extended warranty claims. Lived the problem from inside the TPA industry. Husband worked in insurance last-mile (device repair/returns) for years — deep domain depth. AU contract via The Good Guys + Appliances Online is genuine market entry traction.
profile.revenueModel: TPA fee per claim processed + platform fee to insurers/telcos. Claims are recurring — every device with active cover generates a potential claim event.
profile.risks: Physical operations business — drivers, device collection, repair, returns. Requires humans, vehicles, and logistics infrastructure. Not a pipe play despite the information flow framing.
profile.macroTailwind: Device insurance growing as smartphone penetration hits emerging markets. Telcos bundling device protection as a revenue line. APAC device protection market largely undigitised.

name: Balo
reason: Salesforce-only dependency. Salesforce itself is being disrupted by AI agents — companies are building their own CRM functionality via agents rather than buying Salesforce seats. The expert marketplace thesis relies on Salesforce remaining dominant. Single-vendor concentration was always the key risk; the AI agent wave makes it structural.

profile.whatTheyDo: On-demand expert marketplace for enterprise software support, starting with Salesforce. Connects businesses to vetted top-1% Salesforce experts (250+ globally, less than 4% acceptance rate) for urgent or complex support tasks. Pay-as-you-go model. 14 Salesforce product categories. 230+ companies in 23 countries, $1.3M total transactions, $360K net revenue.
profile.whyFlagged: Information flow pipe embedded in enterprise software operations. 95% repeat revenue and 42% MoM growth at $1.3M ARR. Profitable at 10 months post-launch. Expert network quality (less than 4% acceptance rate) creates real switching cost. 250+ vetted experts, 600+ waitlisted.
profile.founderProfile: Michael Joo (CEO) — 13 years in the Salesforce ecosystem, from developer to building Salesforce agencies. Spearheaded 200+ Salesforce implementations. Classic operator-founder. Yomi Joseph (CTO) — 10+ years building digital products for Target Australia and Tabcorp. Both came into Antler residency with the same startup idea independently.

founders.name: Michael Joo — CEO (13 yrs Salesforce, 200+ implementations)

profile.revenueModel: ~40% take rate on expert sessions. $1.3M+ total transactions, $360K net revenue. 95% repeat project-based work.
profile.risks: Single-vendor concentration (Salesforce). AI agents enabling companies to build their own CRM without Salesforce seats — structural platform risk that accelerated the graveyard decision.
profile.macroTailwind: Enterprise software market growing from $230B to $500B by 2030. Salesforce has 150,000+ customers globally. Shift from large SI retainers to outcome-based flexible expert support.

name: Promosync
reason: Thin moat in a sector we don't love. US and EU players (Kantar, Aforza, Numerator) could enter the AU FMCG market relatively easily. FMCG trade promotion is a declining-margin, retailer-dominated sector. The founder domain expertise is genuine but not enough to offset the moat concern.

profile.whatTheyDo: B2B SaaS platform automating trade promotion management for FMCG brands. Multi-million dollar promotional campaigns run by P&G and Nestle across Woolworths/Coles are currently planned via manual spreadsheets. Promosync replaces that with AI-driven campaign planning, ROI optimisation, and near-real-time performance analytics.
profile.whyFlagged: Information flow pipe inside the FMCG/retailer promotional data exchange. Sits between FMCG suppliers and major retailer scan data — once a brand's promotional history, category data, and retailer relationships are loaded, migration is catastrophic. First AU-native player in a space dominated by US incumbents that don't serve AU well.
profile.founderProfile: Henry Choo (CEO) — 15+ years in FMCG trade promotion management at P&G and Nestle. Pure domain operator. Divyanshu Chauhan (CTO) — serial technical builder at Shippit (raised $30M+), InDebted (Series B), and CSIRO. Strong combination.

founders.name: Henry Choo — CEO (15 yrs P&G + Nestle)

profile.revenueModel: B2B SaaS subscription. Per-brand or per-category pricing. High switching cost once promotional history and retailer data is embedded.
profile.risks: FMCG enterprise sales cycles 6-12 months minimum. US/EU players could enter AU with more resources. Category is declining-margin and retailer-dominated.
profile.macroTailwind: FMCG brands under margin pressure from private label growth. CFOs demanding ROI proof on every promotional dollar.

name: Fennech
reason: Not a startup — founded 2023, UK-domiciled, professional CEO (not founder-led). Founder is not operating as CEO which doesn't fit our founder-operator preference. MAS SFF award is still a signal for the category but Fennech itself is out of scope.

name: fileAI
reason: Missed the entry window. Founded Dec 2020, $20.2M raised across 6 rounds including two Series A tranches ($6.5M Jan 2024, $8M Feb 2025) led by Illuminate Financial + Antler Elevate + Insignia + Investible. Next raise will be Series B — too expensive for meaningful equity at our cheque size. Strong thesis and strong product (AI document workflow automation for financial services) but timing was the issue. We were looking at it in 2025 when it was already well into Series A territory.

name: Light
reason: Missed the entry window. $43M raised across 2 rounds — $13M seed (Jun 2024, Atomico/Cherry/Seedcamp) + $30M Series A (Sep 2025, Balderton Capital lead). Next raise will be Series B, too expensive for meaningful equity. Strong thesis (AI-native general ledger for multinationals) and strong execution, but timing was the issue — in our radar too late.

name: Enrola
reason: Crowded category — AI outbound sales agents is saturated globally (Instantly, Apollo, Clay, Amplemarket, multiple YC companies). Founder met in person, not exciting. Growth pace slow for the category. Passed April 2026.

name: BorderDollar
reason: Presumed dead. Last public activity January 2024 (Antler pre-seed batch). No follow-on raise, no product news, no press coverage in 15+ months. Website returns but is inactive. Cross-border invoice finance is capital-intensive — difficult to build without significant balance sheet backing beyond a pre-seed.

name: Amytis
reason: Product, not a pipe. Amytis is a virtual workspace that unifies scientific data, literature, experiments, and protocols — useful tooling for scientists, not infrastructure through which data or money flows between parties. No switching cost at the platform layer. Also pre-revenue; BGV's first investment is seed-level funding for a product still in development. Tech-for-good cohort implies mission alignment over commercial infrastructure thesis.

profile.fundingNote: BGV Autumn 2025 Tech for Good cohort
profile.whatTheyDo: Virtual workspace for life sciences integrating data, literature, experiments, and protocols into one interactive project graph with AI tools. Aimed at scientists as a productivity and insight layer.
profile.whyFlagged: Information flow adjacent — research data flowing through a central platform could create switching costs if deeply embedded in lab workflows. TechScaler Ones to Watch 2025 mention suggests some early recognition.
profile.founderProfile: Scotland-based founding team. No serial exit or deep domain operator credentials identified in public sources.
profile.revenueModel: SaaS subscription (inferred — product in development, no revenue model publicly disclosed).
profile.risks: Research workspace market is highly competitive (Notion, Benchling, Labguru). Low switching cost if data can be exported. BGV's Tech for Good mandate may constrain commercial aggressiveness.
profile.macroTailwind: Life sciences digitalisation is real and growing, but researcher tooling is a product sale — not infrastructure.

name: Appally

Sits at the HR tool layer, not as infrastructure between parties where switching would be structurally painful. No identified traction or revenue. Pre-seed BGV cohort only.

profile.fundingNote: BGV Autumn 2025 Tech for Good cohort

profile.risks: HR software market is crowded. Disability accommodation automation is a niche. Sustainability of mission-driven business model unclear.
profile.macroTailwind: UK Equality Act 2010 duty to make reasonable adjustments creates compliance demand. Neurodiversity awareness rising in enterprise.

name: Cluso
reason: B2G product, not B2B infrastructure. Cluso is an AI voice survey platform for local government civic consultation — sells to councils, not enterprises. Even if information flows through it, it's a discrete survey product (not infrastructure the buyer depends on for ongoing operations). No network effects between parties. Low switching cost — councils can change survey tools without rebuilding workflows.

profile.fundingNote: BGV Autumn 2025 Tech for Good cohort
profile.whatTheyDo: AI-powered voice survey platform for local government consultations — democratises civic participation by enabling voice-based input from residents at scale.
profile.whyFlagged: AI-native civic data aggregation. UK local government is a captive, underserved market.
profile.risks: GovTech sales cycles are long and painful. Budget constraints at UK councils are severe post-austerity. Survey tooling is inherently low switching-cost.
profile.macroTailwind: UK government digital transformation push creates demand for modern civic engagement tools.

Sits in the clean energy/consumer advisory space. Not a pipe. Heat pump market is early adoption in UK; consumer AI assistant on top of it is a thin wedge with no structural switching cost.

profile.whyFlagged: UK heat pump market is policy-supported; information gap between homeowners and heat pump installers is real.
profile.revenueModel: Unknown — potentially installer referral fees or energy company partnerships.
profile.risks: Consumer advisory AI has low defensibility. UK heat pump adoption is growing slowly despite government subsidies. Revenue model unclear.
profile.macroTailwind: UK government heat pump target (600K/year by 2028) creates market. Boiler Upgrade Scheme subsidies are pulling demand.

Founder (Gracie Broom) is a design graduate with no prior exit. Explicitly stated 'still collecting data' — zero paying customers at time of Imperial VCC win (Nov 2025).
